items.title: [Bug]: `BaseThinkingReasoningParser.extract_reasoning` silently discards output text when `<think>` appears mid-stream
items.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```text
vLLM:            0.25.1 (docker image vllm/vllm-openai:v0.25.1)
Model:           poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-INT4
Flags:           --reasoning-parser poolside_v1 --tool-call-parser poolside_v1
                 --enable-auto-tool-choice
                 --default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true}'
GPU:             8x RTX 3090 (SM86), TP4
```

`collect_env.py` output not attached because the deployment runs inside the
official container; the affected code path is pure Python string handling and
does not depend on hardware or backend.

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`BaseThinkingReasoningParser.extract_reasoning` drops a portion of the model's
output. The dropped text is returned in **neither** `content` **nor**
`reasoning` — it is silently lost.

Affected are parsers that inherit `BaseThinkingReasoningParser` **without**
overriding `extract_reasoning`. Checked on `main`:

| Parser | inherits base | own `extract_reasoning` | affected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek_r1` | yes | no | **yes** |
| `poolside_v1` (via `deepseek_v3` → `deepseek_r1`) | – | no | **yes** |
| `minimax_m3` | yes | yes | no |
| `ernie45` | yes | yes | no |

#### The code

`vllm/reasoning/basic_parsers.py`, lines 157-181 on `main`:

```python
def extract_reasoning(
    self, model_output: str, request: "ChatCompletionRequest | ResponsesRequest"
) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
    # Check if the start token is present in the model output, remove it
    # if it is present.
    model_output_parts = model_output.partition(self.start_token)
    model_output = (
        model_output_parts[2] if model_output_parts[1] else model_output_parts[0]
    )
    ...
```

`model_output_parts[0]` — everything **before** the matched `<think>` — is bound
to nothing. When the match succeeds, that prefix is discarded and never appears
in either return value.

The match is unanchored: `str.partition` finds the **first** occurrence anywhere
in the output. It has no notion of position, of JSON string context, or of
tool-call markup. A `<think>` the model produced as *data* is indistinguishable
from one produced as a *delimiter*.

Note this is a **string** match, so it fires regardless of tokenisation. The
model does not need to emit the reasoning special token; ordinary BPE pieces that
decode to `<think>` are enough.

#### Reproduction

Any prompt that makes a reasoning model write `<think>` in its answer will do.
Asking it to explain what the tag means is the natural case:

```bash
curl -s http://$ENDPOINT/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "'"$MODEL"'",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content":
    "Explain in two sentences what the tag consisting of a less-than sign, the letters t h i n k, and a greater-than sign means in a chat template. Write the tag out once."}],
  "max_tokens": 1200,
  "temperature": 0,
  "return_token_ids": true}'
```

Then compare the true model output against what the API returned. Detokenising
`token_ids` gives the raw generation, so nothing has to be inferred:

```python
raw = detokenize(response.token_ids)          # what the model actually produced
returned = len(content) + len(reasoning)      # what the API handed back
```

Measured, three runs at `temperature 0`:

| Run | `<think>` in raw output | raw | content | reasoning | lost |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | at char 680 | 2078 | 287 | 1084 | **707** |
| 2 | not written by the model | 1244 | – | – | 0 |
| 3 | at char 658 | 3805 | 364 | 2756 | **685** |

In runs 1 and 3 the first 680 / 658 characters of the reasoning are gone. Their
opening is:

```text
'Okay, the user is asking me to explain what the sequence of lowercase letters
"t h i n k" in a chat template means, and ...'
```

Verified explicitly: this text is a substring of neither `content` nor
`reasoning`. Run 2 is not a counter-example — the model simply did not write the
tag that time, so the code path was not reached.

#### Why this matters beyond the obvious

`DelegatingParser.parse` runs reasoning extraction across the **entire** raw
output before the tool-call parser gets to split arguments
(`vllm/parser/abstract_parser.py:793`):

```python
reasoning, content = self.extract_reasoning(model_output, request)
tool_calls, content = self._extract_tool_calls(content=content, ...)
```

So a `<think>` occurring inside a tool-call argument is consumed before anything
that understands tool calls has seen it. The tool parser is handed only the
remainder.

The practical failure mode is a coding agent editing source code that contains
`<think>` as a string literal — for example a chat-template or output-parser
implementation. The edit silently does nothing, or arrives truncated.

#### Affected versions

`vllm/reasoning/basic_parsers.py` is byte-identical at `v0.25.1`, `v0.26.0` and
`main` (verified by sha256). The behaviour is unchanged across all three.

#### The fix already exists in this repository

`MiniMaxM3ReasoningParser` overrides `extract_reasoning` and handles exactly this
case correctly (`vllm/reasoning/minimax_m3_reasoning_parser.py`):

```python
content_before, _, after_start = model_output.partition(self.start_token)
reasoning, end, content_after = after_start.partition(self.end_token)
if not end:
    return reasoning, content_before or None

return reasoning, (content_before + content_after) or None
```

The prefix is captured as `content_before` and concatenated onto the content
rather than dropped. Lifting this into `BaseThinkingReasoningParser` would fix
`deepseek_r1` and its delegates and let `minimax_m3` drop its override.

#### Suggested direction

Two separable problems:

1. **The discard is unambiguous data loss.** Whatever the intended semantics, a
   parser should not route text to neither output field. The `minimax_m3`
   treatment above is the obvious in-repo precedent.

2. **The unanchored search is the deeper issue.** The intent appears to be
   "strip a leading `<think>` wrapper". Anchoring the match to the start of the
   generation would express that intent and would make a mid-stream occurrence
   harmless. Parsers that moved to the `ParserEngine` design (`qwen3`,
   `glm47_moe`) do not have this problem, because a single state machine sees
   reasoning markers and tool-call markup together and knows which region of the
   stream it is in.

I am happy to open a PR for (1) if that direction is acceptable.

#### What I did not verify

- Only reproduced with `poolside_v1`. `deepseek_r1` shares the identical base
  class and the same `extract_reasoning`, so it should behave the same, but I did
  not run it.
- The streaming path (`extract_reasoning_streaming`, same file) has a separate
  single-special-token skip at lines 112-116 that also returns `None`. I have not
  characterised it and it is not part of this report.
- I have not checked whether the Rust frontend shares this logic.

#### Related but distinct

- **#48663** — `minimax_m3` splitting structured-output JSON at a `<mm:think>`
  written as data. Same *class* of problem, different parser. As shown above the
  non-streaming `minimax_m3` path preserves the prefix, so that report concerns a
  different code path.
- **#48863 / #48865** — same function, different line: misclassification of
  output that contains no think block at all (`return model_output, None` when
  `end_token` is absent). That fix does not address the discarded prefix.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I have searched existing issues and could not find this reported.
- [x] I have made sure the reproduction is minimal and self-contained.

items.title: [Bug]: Gemma4 tool parser (non-streaming): finish_reason=tool_calls with empty tool_calls array — model's move silently lost under concurrent load
items.body:
## Symptom

On intermittent occasions under concurrent agentic load, a **non-streaming** `/v1/chat/completions` request served with the Gemma4 tool-call parser returns:

- `choices[0].finish_reason == "tool_calls"`
- `choices[0].message.tool_calls == []` (empty array — not null, not missing)
- `choices[0].message.content` empty or a short prose echo

i.e. the engine *signals* that the model made a tool move, but the parsed calls are lost and the raw text is not surfaced either — the model's move is silently swallowed. An agentic client has nothing to execute and nothing to re-parse.

## Environment

- vLLM **0.26.0**, torch 2.11.0+cu130
- Model: `google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-w4a16-ct` (compressed-tensors W4A16; also reproduced on the 26B QAT sibling)
- 8× GPU, TP8
- Serve command:

```
vllm serve google/gemma-4-31B-it-qat-w4a16-ct \
  --served-model-name nexa-small \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser gemma4 --reasoning-parser gemma4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len 131072 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-seqs 8 \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
```

## Frequency / conditions

Multi-agent orchestration platform, several concurrent conversations with tool specs (10-40 tools offered per request), long prompts (10k-100k tokens). Roughly **5 occurrences over ~2 days of continuous agentic traffic** (thousands of requests) — rare, but each occurrence breaks the consuming agent's turn (we had to build a client-side typed retry barrier around it).

Client-side capture at the moment of failure (our audit layer): `finish_reason="tool_calls"`, `raw tool_calls=[]`, content head empty/echo. The same request retried immediately usually succeeds, which points at a parser/race condition rather than a prompt problem.

## Possibly related

- #39392 (Gemma4 tool-call-parser produces `<pad>` tokens under concurrent requests) — same parser, also concurrency-correlated, different visible symptom.
- #44522 (closed — parser leaked raw tokens in streaming). Ours is the non-streaming lane: nothing is leaked; the move disappears entirely.

## Expected behavior

When the Gemma4 parser cannot extract any tool call from a completion that triggered the tool-call stop condition, either (a) the raw model text should be preserved in `message.content` so the client can recover, or (b) `finish_reason` should not claim `tool_calls`. `finish_reason=tool_calls` with an empty array and empty content loses the model's output with no recovery path.

items.title: [Bugfix] MiniMax-M3 fp8_e5m2 KV cache on SM80 (A100/A800): admit the format Triton can read, fix the CUDA-graph KV corruption
items.body:
Draft port of the SM80 fp8-KV enablement for MiniMax-M3 onto current main. Fixes #50881.

**In this draft already:** the Triton attention backend guard now admits `fp8_e5m2` on SM80 — Triton there can read fp8e5; it is only fp8e4nv (e4m3) that needs SM89+. e4m3 stays rejected below SM89, and the error now suggests `fp8_e5m2` to Ampere users instead of a bf16 downgrade.

**Coming with hardware verification on 8xA800 (tomorrow):**
- route dense-layer KV writes through the CUDA `reshape_and_cache_flash` (software fp8 convert) instead of the Triton kernel that needs native fp8e4nv;
- make `MiniMaxM3SparseAttention._insert_kv` CUDA-graph-safe via `@eager_break_during_capture` — the root cause of the fp8+graph garbage diagnosed in #50881;
- the remaining SM89 guards on this path, plus needle/1M-window/GPQA numbers re-measured on main.

Diagnosis, per-kernel numerical probes, and the fork-based patch set this ports from: https://github.com/Hakureirm/minimax-m3-ampere

Marked draft until the full set and the on-hardware verification land.

items.title: [Bug]: override-generation-config silently ignores presence_penalty / frequency_penalty (missing from available_params whitelist)
items.body:
### Your current environment
The output of vllm collect-env ```text ============================== System Info ============================== OS : Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64) GCC version : (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.3) 11.4.0 Libc version : glibc-2.35 ============================== PyTorch Info ============================== PyTorch version : 2.11.0+cu130 Is debug build : False CUDA used to build PyTorch : 13.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : N/A ============================== Python Environment ============================== Python version : 3.12.13 (main, Mar 4 2026, 09:23:07) [GCC 11.4.0] (64-bit runtime) Python platform : Linux-7.0.0-28-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.35 ============================== CUDA / GPU Info ============================== Is CUDA available : True CUDA runtime version : 13.0.88 GPU models and configuration : GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 GPU 1: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Nvidia driver version : 595.71.05 ============================== CPU Info ============================== Architecture: x86_64 CPU(s): 44 Model name: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2696 v4 @ 2.20GHz NUMA node(s): 1 ============================== Versions of relevant libraries ============================== [pip3] vllm==0.24.0 [pip3] flashinfer-python==0.6.12 [pip3] numpy==2.2.6 [pip3] nvidia-cublas==13.1.0.3 [pip3] nvidia-cuda-nvrtc==13.0.88 ```
### 🐛 Describe the bug `--override-generation-config` is intended to set server-side default sampling parameters that apply when the client does not send a value for that parameter. It works for `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `min_p`, `repetition_penalty` and `max_new_tokens`, but **silently ignores `presence_penalty` and `frequency_penalty`** — both are missing from the `available_params` whitelist in `ModelConfig.get_diff_sampling_param()` (`vllm/config/model.py`). No warning is emitted, and the sampler always falls back to `0.0`. This is the same class of silent-drop bug as #45591 (where `eos_token_id` was dropped by the same whitelist mechanism and later fixed). ```bash # Server-side default sampling params: vllm serve /path/to/model \ --generation-config vllm \ --override-generation-config '{"presence_penalty":1.5,"temperature":0.6,"top_p":0.95}' \ --enable-log-requests # Client request that does NOT send presence_penalty: curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":8}' ``` Observed server log (`--enable-log-requests`): ```text SamplingParams(... presence_penalty=0.0, ..., temperature=0.6, top_p=0.95, ...) # ^^ configured default 1.5 never applied ``` `temperature`/`top_p` from `--override-generation-config` are applied, but `presence_penalty` is not. Expected behavior: `presence_penalty` (and `frequency_penalty`) configured in `--override-generation-config` should be applied as server-side defaults, exactly like `temperature`/`top_p`. They are standard sampling parameters of both `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/responses`, and the only sampling parameters in this whitelist that accept a client value but have no server-default path. Root cause location: `vllm/config/model.py`, `ModelConfig.get_diff_sampling_param()`: ```python available_params = [ "repetition_penalty", "temperature", "top_k", "top_p", "min_p", "max_new_tokens", ] ``` Verified present on `v0.24.0` (this env), still present on `v0.26.0` and on `main`. Impact: deployments that rely on server-side default penalties (e.g. an LLM gateway in front of vLLM that does not forward penalty fields) cannot get presence/frequency penalty applied, causing output repetition / tool-call loops that are very hard to diagnose. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Bugfix] serving_llama70B_tp4 benchmark was silently running at tensor_parallel_size=1

labels.name: ready

items.body:
## Purpose

While building an AMD-specific variant of the performance-benchmark test configs (`serving-tests-rocm.json`, mirroring `serving-tests.json`), verifying the copied `serving_llama70B_tp4_random_128_128` entry through the actual `merge_serving_tests_stream` merge logic in `run-performance-benchmarks.sh` surfaced that its `server_parameters` never sets `tensor_parallel_size`. It silently inherits `tensor_parallel_size: 1` from the file's `defaults` block instead.

This test has presumably been running as `tp1`, not `tp4`, on the continuous `perf.vllm.ai` benchmark this whole time — the test name and the fixed 8192 `max_num_batched_tokens`/`async_scheduling` server args are set up for a 4-GPU run, but the actual TP degree silently defaulted to 1.

## Changes

- `.buildkite/performance-benchmarks/tests/serving-tests.json`: add `"tensor_parallel_size": 4` to `serving_llama70B_tp4_random_128_128`'s `server_parameters`.

## Why not duplicate

Searched open PRs touching this file. #46870 ("fix: remove stray duplicate from serving benchmark config") also touches `serving-tests.json`, but at a different, unrelated entry (`serving_llama8B_tp1_sharegpt`, ~line 28) — removes a stray duplicate JSON fragment causing invalid JSON. That PR's new `check-json` pre-commit hook validates JSON syntax only, so it wouldn't catch this bug either (this file is, and was, syntactically valid — just semantically wrong on one field). No line-range or content overlap with this change.

No open issue or PR references `serving_llama70B_tp4` or a missing `tensor_parallel_size` in this file.

## Test Plan / Result

Verified through the actual merge logic the runner script uses (`merge_serving_tests_stream`, which applies the `defaults` → per-test override merge), not just visual inspection:

```bash
# before the fix:
$ merge_serving_tests_stream tests/serving-tests.json | jq -c 'select(.test_name=="serving_llama70B_tp4_random_128_128") | .server_parameters.tensor_parallel_size'
1

# after the fix:
$ merge_serving_tests_stream tests/serving-tests.json | jq -c 'select(.test_name=="serving_llama70B_tp4_random_128_128") | .server_parameters.tensor_parallel_size'
4
```

Also confirmed:
- `jq . tests/serving-tests.json` — still valid JSON.
- All 7 test names in the file still present and merge cleanly after the change (no regression to the other entries).
- `pre-commit run --files .buildkite/performance-benchmarks/tests/serving-tests.json` passes.

---

*AI assistance disclosure: found and fixed with Claude Code, surfaced as a side effect of validating a separate AMD-specific benchmark config change against the actual merge/parsing logic in `run-performance-benchmarks.sh` rather than by inspection. I reviewed the one-line change and independently re-ran the before/after verification myself.*

items.title: fix(uva): fix silent input corruption and remote DoS under GPU CC
items.body:
Under GPU Confidential Computing (CC), torch.Tensor.is_pinned() returns false for genuinely pinned memory because the CUDA runtime classifies the pointer as "Managed" instead of "Host".  This caused get_cuda_view_from_cpu_tensor to take a detached-buffer fallback that broke the live-alias contract used by the V2 model runner's UVA buffers, resulting in:

1. Silent input corruption: every request fed all-zero tokens to the model while returning HTTP 200.
2. Remote DoS: the degenerate generation underflowed the async scheduler's num_output_placeholders accounting, crashing the EngineCore with AssertionError on a single long-context request.

Changes:
- cuda_view.cu: try cudaHostGetDevicePointer unconditionally first, falling back to the alloc+copy path only when it fails. This removes the is_pinned() gate and lets the CUDA API itself determine whether zero-copy is possible.
- platform_utils.py: add verify_uva_coherence() startup probe that validates write-after-map coherence at worker init (defense-in-depth).
- gpu_worker.py: call the coherence probe when UVA + V2 model runner are active.
- async_scheduler.py: replace the hard assert on num_output_placeholders >= 0 with a graceful clamp-and-stop, so degenerate generation degrades gracefully instead of killing the engine.
- tests: add UVA coherence test and async scheduler underflow test.

items.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Kimi-K3 Fix KDA NaN on mixed batches and racy autotune config
items.body:
## Purpose
For Kimi-K3, there are two correctness bugs on the ROCm Kimi-K3 KDA path.

- `KimiGatedDeltaNetAttention._forward` sends the decode sequences of a mixed decode+prefill non-speculative batch through the KDA chunk kernel `chunk_kda_with_fused_gate`. The chunk kernel treats each decode as length=1 sequence, and returns NaN for them. This PR separates the decode out of the mixed batch and pass them to `fused_recurrent_kda`.
- `recompute_w_u_fwd_kernel` autotunes the configuration of `num_stages=4`. This configuration, particularly in combination with `num_warps=4`, is racy for this kernel, and can silently produce large (e.g. ~1e38) garbage values that corrupts the downstream. This PR addresses this by leaving the `num_stages=4` out in autotuning so that it doesn't land on the erroneous configuration.

items.title: [Bug]: gfx1100 (RDNA3): first-call non-determinism + long-seq corruption from Triton paged-attention fallback (ROCm 7.14)
items.body:
> **TL;DR** — On **gfx1100/RDNA3**, vLLM 0.25.1's **Triton paged-attention fallback** is (A) **non-deterministic on the first `generate()` call of a process** (at *any* sequence length — not a long-seq threshold) and (B) **garbled at long context**. The ROCm CK custom paged kernel is gated out because the model's decoder is GQA with **`gqa_ratio=2`** (CK requires `≥3`), forcing the Triton `kernel_paged_attention_2d`. A warmup call fixes (A) but not (B); **transformers `sdpa` is deterministic + correct on the same stack**. Full repro (3 scripts + build note + expected outputs): https://gist.github.com/AIwork4me/030fc6a872de36197178c9e8217949d1 ### Your current environment
The output of collect_env.py (trimmed) ```text OS : Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (x86_64) PyTorch version : 2.11.0+rocm7.14.0 ROCM used to build PyTorch : 7.14.60850 Python version : 3.12.3 Is CUDA available : True GPU models and configuration : 4x AMD Radeon Pro W7900D (gfx1100, RDNA3) HIP runtime version : 7.14.60850 MIOpen runtime version : 3.5.2 [pip3] torch==2.11.0+rocm7.14.0 [pip3] transformers==5.13.0 [pip3] triton==3.7.1+git0263a6a6.rocm7.14.0 vLLM Version : 0.25.1 (built from source, PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1100) ```
Note: vLLM 0.25.1 is **built from source** on ROCm 7.14 (no official gfx1100 wheel at this version), and the hardware is **RDNA3 (gfx1100)**. Reproducing requires gfx1100/RDNA3; **gfx1100 (Radeon Pro W7900) cloud instances** are available from AMD-Radeon GPU providers such as [Radeon Cloud](https://radeon-global.anruicloud.com/) (no affiliation — linked only to lower the hardware barrier, not an endorsement). Build caveat: the implicated `kernel_paged_attention_2d` is a pure-Triton kernel JIT-compiled at runtime, but in this env vLLM's pre-compiled HIP kernels were built against 7.2.1 system headers and run on the 7.14 torch — if a cleanly-7.14-built vLLM does not reproduce, that mismatch is the first thing to rule out (details in the gist README). See the scope question at the end. ### 🐛 Describe the bug On **gfx1100 (RDNA3, Radeon Pro W7900D)**, vLLM 0.25.1 serving a VLM (`tencent/HunyuanOCR`, `HunYuanVLForConditionalGeneration`) shows **two distinct problems**, both rooted in the ROCm paged-attention **Triton fallback** that vLLM selects on gfx1100 (the CK custom paged kernel is gated out — see root-cause trail): **Symptom A — first-call non-determinism (not length-gated).** The **first** `generate()` call in a process produces different output from subsequent identical calls. With greedy decoding, three identical (image, prompt) runs give `sha8 = ba29b5a1, fd0cc624, fd0cc624` — run 0 (the cold/JIT-compiled first call) diverges, runs 1 & 2 are identical. This reproduces at **both** ~15k vision tokens (2048×1920 page) **and** ~3.8k tokens (1024×960 page) — i.e. it is **not** a long-sequence-threshold effect. A single warmup `generate()` before the measured runs eliminates it: after warmup, three identical runs are byte-identical (`sha8 = fd0cc624, fd0cc624, fd0cc624`). **Symptom B — incorrect (garbled) output at long sequence, even when deterministic.** At full resolution (~15k vision tokens), the warmed/deterministic vLLM output is garbled OCR (`lial Oswuamtntnralglyy Flinamie …`) and does **not** contain the ground-truth text, whereas **transformers** with `attn_implementation="sdpa"` on the **same** ROCm 7.14 / gfx1100 / torch 2.11 stack, on the **same** image, is deterministic **and correct** (GT title present). So the ROCm stack *can* do correct long-sequence bf16 attention for this model; vLLM's path cannot. #### Minimal repro ```python from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams # 2048x1920 page = 15360 ViT patches (long-seq case). Use 1024x960 = 3840 for the short-seq case. W, H = 2048, 1920 im = Image.new("RGB", (W, H), "white"); d = ImageDraw.Draw(im) f = ImageFont.truetype("/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans-Bold.ttf", 96) d.text((120, 120), "Quarterly Financial Summary", font=f, fill="black") im.save("/tmp/page.png") PROMPT = ("提取文档图片中正文的所有信息用markdown格式表示，其中页眉、页脚部分忽略，" "表格用html格式表达，文档中公式用latex格式表示，按照阅读顺序组织进行解析。") llm = LLM(model="tencent/HunyuanOCR", dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=32768, gpu_memory_utilization=0.90, enforce_eager=True, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1}, trust_remote_code=True) sp = SamplingParams(temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, top_k=-1, max_tokens=1024, repetition_penalty=1.08) prompt = llm.get_tokenizer().apply_chat_template( [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "image"}, {"type": "text", "text": PROMPT}]}], tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True) img = Image.open("/tmp/page.png").convert("RGB") for i in range(3): # Symptom A: run 0 differs from runs 1 & 2 print(i, llm.generate({"prompt": prompt, "multi_modal_data": {"image": img}}, sampling_params=sp, use_tqdm=False)[0].outputs[0].text[:80]) ``` Observed (3× identical input, full-res): ```text sha8 = ba29b5a1, fd0cc624, fd0cc624 # run 0 != run 1 == run 2 byte-identical: False GT title present in any run: False # garbled even on the deterministic (warmed) runs ``` #### Evidence summary | experiment (greedy ×3 identical input) | sha8 | deterministic? | correct? | |---|---|---|---| | full-res (15360 tok), no warmup | `ba29b5a1, fd0cc624, fd0cc624` | ❌ no (symptom A) | ❌ garbled (symptom B) | | short-seq (3840 tok), no warmup | `f00c87f2, f31888d4, f31888d4` | ❌ no (symptom A is not length-gated) | (image too small to judge) | | full-res (15360 tok), 1 warmup then ×3 | `fd0cc624, fd0cc624, fd0cc624` | ✅ yes (warmup fixes A) | ❌ still garbled (B remains) | | transformers `sdpa`, full-res | `a313e63a ×3` | ✅ yes | ✅ correct | #### Root-cause trail (what I verified) 1. **It is not the vision encoder.** Forcing the ViT/mm-encoder backend to `TORCH_SDPA` (which routes through `F.scaled_dot_product_attention`, via `mm_encoder_attn_backend="TORCH_SDPA"`) changed the output **zero** — byte-identical to the default `FLASH_ATTN` (Triton) ViT path (same sha8s). So the ViT is deterministic in both backends and is not the source. By elimination the divergent path is the **decoder**. 2. **The decoder runs through vLLM's standard paged-attention path.** `HunYuanVLForConditionalGeneration` (`vllm/model_executor/models/hunyuan_vision.py`) uses a HunYuan V1 language backbone (`hunyuan_v1.py: HunYuanAttention`), which builds a **standard `Attention`** (head_dim=128, num_kv_heads=8 → **gqa_ratio=2**), not `MLAAttention`. 3. **The ROCm CK custom paged-attention kernel is gated out**, so vLLM uses the Triton kernel. On gfx1100, `use_rocm_custom_paged_attention()` (`vllm/platforms/rocm.py`) requires `gqa_ratio∈[3,16]`; **gqa_ratio=2 fails**, so the CK kernel is disabled and vLLM falls back to **Triton `kernel_paged_attention_2d`** (`vllm/v1/attention/ops/chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py`). The run logs confirm both: ``` WARNING [chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py:419] Cannot use ROCm custom paged attention kernel, falling back to Triton implementation. WARNING [jit_monitor.py:129] Triton kernel JIT compilation during inference: kernel_paged_attention_2d. ... consider extending warmup to cover this shape/config. ``` Symptom A (first-call non-determinism) lines up with that kernel being JIT-compiled on first use (hence warmup eliminates it). Symptom B (long-seq corruption) lines up with that Triton kernel not matching the (correct) torch-SDPA numerics at long bf16 sequences on gfx1100. #### Ask 1. **First-call determinism (symptom A):** vLLM's own `jit_monitor` says to "extend warmup to cover this shape/config." Can engine warmup be extended to cover the paged-attention decode shape so the **first** real request is deterministic (not just the second onward)? 2. **Long-seq correctness (symptom B):** can the Triton `kernel_paged_attention_2d` numerics on gfx1100 be made to match torch-SDPA at long bf16 sequences — or can the **CK custom paged kernel** be extended to `gqa_ratio=2` (and the HunYuan V1 GQA config) so RDNA3 uses the deterministic CK path instead of the Triton fallback? 3. **Scope:** gfx1100/RDNA3 is a consumer GPU. Is paged-attention determinism/correctness on RDNA3 within vLLM's ROCm support scope (which I understand to be CDNA/MI-series focused)? If RDNA3 is community-supported only, happy to move/dupe this to the right place. Happy to attach the rendered page image, raw token ids, or full run logs on request. Thanks! > Note: vLLM 0.25.1 is not a HunyuanOCR-model-card-listed vLLM version (card lists 0.18.1 / nightly / 0.13). I'm reporting because the failure looks like a platform/kernel-architecture issue (gfx1100 paged-attention), not a model-compat one.

items.title: [Misc] Warn when --block-size is silently discarded by backend alignment

labels.name: verified
labels.description: Run pre-commit for new contributors without triggering other tests

items.body:
## Purpose

`Platform._align_hybrid_block_size` computes the kernel block alignment as `max(backend_minimum, cache_config.block_size)`, further floored at 128 for MLA. When the backend minimum (or MLA floor) exceeds the requested value, an explicit `--block-size` is silently discarded — and the log line further down reports the *derived* value, never the input that produced it, so an accepted and a discarded `--block-size` look identical in the logs. On a hybrid model this derived value also fixes the prefix-cache match granularity (GCD over group block sizes), so two otherwise identical configurations differing only in whether `--block-size` cleared the floor can silently diverge in cache-hit behavior. One such pair took most of a day to diagnose: the two lanes' KV cache pools differed by ~20% (1,950,541 vs. 2,332,440 tokens) with nothing in either log explaining why.

This PR adds a one-time warning when that happens. It fires only when `--block-size` was explicitly passed, and only when the resulting alignment is identical to what `update_block_size_for_backend`'s Phase 1 would have picked with the flag absent (via `backend_cls.get_preferred_block_size`) — not simply whenever the value is at or below the backend minimum. That distinction matters: a backend whose preferred size exceeds its own minimum (e.g. FlashAttention on XPU, floor 16 / preferred 64) has its outcome changed by an explicit low `--block-size`, since it suppresses Phase 1's preferred-size selection, so that case must not be flagged as having no effect. This is a logging-only change; it does not alter any computed block size.

I checked for duplicate and overlapping open PRs (`gh pr list --search` on
"block size warning", "block_size alignment", "kernel_block_alignment" and
"preferred block size"). Two are adjacent and neither overlaps.

#48499 touches the same file for the neighbouring case: a user-specified
`--block-size` the active backend does not support at all, which it rejects
early instead of letting it fail after model load. This change is about a
value the backend *does* accept, which alignment then silently raises, so the
flag is honoured as far as validation is concerned and still has no effect —
#48499 would not fire on it, and this warning would not fire on #48499's case.
The two are complementary, and I am happy to fold this into #48499 if the
maintainers would rather have one change in that function.

#48402 also warns about a block size, but on a different condition in a
different file: prefix caching going inert when the block size exceeds
`max_model_len`.

I used AI assistance (Cursor) to draft, test, and validate this change, and I
reviewed every changed line before submitting.

New unit tests in `tests/platforms/test_interface.py`, wired into CI via `.buildkite/test_areas/misc.yaml` (`pytest -v -s platforms`). They mock the attention backend and a hybrid model to exercise `_align_hybrid_block_size` directly, and separately drive the same scenarios through the public `update_block_size_for_backend` entry point so Phase 1's skip-on-explicit-flag behavior is exercised rather than bypassed.

On v0.26.0, a Chat Completions request with a **named** forced tool choice
(`tool_choice: {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "..."}}`) returns
HTTP 200 with a plain prose answer: `finish_reason: "stop"`, `tool_calls:
null`. The forced contract is accepted and then silently not enforced. The
model answers from its training data instead of calling the tool.

The same request on v0.21.0 returns the expected function call.

`tool_choice: "required"` works correctly on **both** versions, so the
regression is specific to the named-function mode. This looks related to the
legacy→engine-based gemma4 parser replacement (#45588 / #45553, first
released in v0.24.0), and is the Chat Completions sibling of #49712 (named
tool_choice silently ignored on the Responses API for unsupported XML
parsers).

Silent non-enforcement is worse than an error: callers that rely on a forced
call (e.g. a mandatory retrieval step, or a terminal/checkpoint function)
get a 200 with prose and no signal that the contract was broken.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VLLM_URL/chat/completions" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "google/gemma-4-26b-A4B-it",
    "temperature": 0,
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "How many days of paid leave do employees get in France?"}
    ],
    "tools": [{
      "type": "function",
      "function": {
        "name": "lookup_knowledge_base",
        "description": "Look up the knowledge base and return the passages that answer a question.",
        "parameters": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"query": {"type": "string", "minLength": 1}},
          "required": ["query"],
          "additionalProperties": false
        }
      }
    }],
    "tool_choice": {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "lookup_knowledge_base"}}
  }'
```

### Result on v0.21.0 (expected behavior)

```json
{
  "choices": [{
    "finish_reason": "stop",
    "message": {
      "content": "",
      "tool_calls": [{
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
          "name": "lookup_knowledge_base",
          "arguments": "{\n  \"query\": \"number of paid leave days for employees in France\"\n}"
        }
      }]
    }
  }]
}
```

### Result on v0.26.0 (bug)

```json
{
  "choices": [{
    "finish_reason": "stop",
    "message": {
      "content": "In France, employees are legally entitled to a minimum of five weeks of paid leave [... full prose answer, ~300 tokens ...]",
      "tool_calls": null
    }
  }]
}
```

Same request, `tool_choice: "required"` instead of the named form — works on
both versions:

```json
{
  "choices": [{
    "finish_reason": "tool_calls",
    "message": {
      "content": "",
      "tool_calls": [{
        "type": "function",
        "function": {
          "name": "lookup_knowledge_base",
          "arguments": "{\"query\": \"paid leave days France employees\"}"
        }
      }]
    }
  }]
}
```

## Expected behavior

Either enforce the named function call (as v0.21.0 does and as `"required"`
still does), or reject the request with an explicit error if the parser
cannot enforce named tool choices — never a silent 200 with prose.

## Related issues

- #49712 — Responses API silently ignores named tool_choice for unsupported XML tool parsers (same symptom class, different API/parser)
- #40528 — forced tool_choice crashes with AssertionError when reasoning_parser consumes all content
- #45588 / #45553 — the gemma4 parser replacement between which this behavior changed

## AI assistance disclosure

This report was drafted with AI assistance (Claude). All findings were produced and verified by a human: every reproduction was run against the two live deployments described above (raw curl, no SDK), the outputs pasted here are unedited actual responses, and the related-issues triage was reviewed manually.

### 🐛 Describe the bug With the FlexAttention backend, the paged K/V element offset inside the generated Triton kernel is computed in **int32**. Once `num_gpu_blocks` reaches `2**31 / (block_size * 2 * num_kv_heads * head_size)` the product wraps negative and the kernel addresses memory ~4 GiB *below* the K/V base. For a `num_kv_heads=8, head_size=128, block_size=16` cache that bound is exactly **65,536 blocks**. Nothing validates `num_gpu_blocks` against it. The failure has **two modes**, decided only by whether the wrapped address happens to be mapped: an `illegal memory access`, or **no error at all** — the kernel silently reads the neighbouring allocation and returns wrong attention output. The faulting address sits ~90 GB below the other live pointers. ### Where the int32 comes from `vllm/v1/attention/backends/flex_attention.py` builds `kv_indices` as int32 (still true on `main` as of 2026-07-30): ```python kv_indices = unique_static_unsorted((used_pages_padded.long()), M=self.num_blocks).to(torch.int32) kv_indices = copy_to_persistent(self.persistent_kv_indices, kv_indices) self.persistent_kv_indices = torch.empty( self.max_num_query_groups, self.max_num_kv_indices, dtype=torch.int32, device=self.device) ``` so every downstream term stays in that dtype (`kv_start = kv_indices * block_size`, `ptr = K + offs_n * stride_kn`). The generated kernel does define `INDEX_DTYPE = tl.int64`, but only the **output store** indices go through it; the K/V gather offsets do not. What makes the offset exceed the K tensor's own `numel` is that **K and V share one buffer**, so the K view's maximum linear offset spans the *whole* buffer while its `numel` is only half of it. Inductor appears to pick the index dtype from `numel` (~1.12e9 here, which fits int32) rather than from the stride-derived maximum offset (~2.24e9, which does not). ⚠️ **The packing axis differs between releases — this needs updating before submitting.** Our environment (`0.23.1rc1.dev813+g344609ab1`) packs on a dedicated dim and splits with `unbind`: ```python # flex_attention.py:133 (dev813, what we measured) return (num_blocks, 2, block_size, num_kv_heads, head_size) # flex_attention.py:1245 / :1350 key_cache, value_cache = kv_cache.unbind(1) ``` `main` (2026-07-30) packs into the content dim instead: ```python # K and V are packed into the content dim: logical (B, H, N, 2*hs). return (num_blocks, num_kv_heads, block_size, 2 * head_size) ... kv_cache = kv_cache.transpose(1, 2) key_cache, value_cache = kv_cache.split(hs, dim=-1) ``` The bound is **unchanged** by this, because in both layouts the buffer holds `num_blocks * block_size * (2 * num_kv_heads * head_size)` elements and the K view's maximum offset reaches the far end of it: ``` max_safe_num_gpu_blocks = 2**31 // (block_size * 2 * num_kv_heads * head_size) = 2**31 // (16 * 2 * 8 * 128) = 65,536 ``` but the *per-token* stride differs, so **the `main` derivation above is analytical — we measured the `unbind` layout, not the packed one.** Re-run snippet (b) against `main`'s layout before filing. Bisecting one property at a time on the layout we did measure, the shared buffer is the only necessary condition: replacing the two strided views with separate contiguous K/V tensors halves the stride and doubles the bound. `kv_indices` contiguity, Q layout, `enable_gqa`, `Q_LEN` alignment and `KV_LEN` magnitude are all irrelevant. Also note `kv_cache_utils.py` now has a `_use_packed_kv_cache_config` / `_get_packed_kv_cache_layout` path returning a `block_stride`; whether that changes the effective stride for this backend is **not checked**. ### Who is exposed `num_blocks = available_memory // (group_size * page_size)` where `group_size = max(len(g.layer_names) for g in kv_cache_groups)` — the number of memory pools the hybrid allocator creates. **Exposure grows as `group_size` shrinks**, so models whose layers split into many KV cache groups are the most exposed; a uniform single-group model needs proportionally more memory to reach the bound. Being upfront about our own trigger: we reached `num_gpu_blocks = 70,315` with an **out-of-tree** backend whose per-layer window config split 36 layers into 4 groups (`group_size = 9`, 37.56 GiB of KV cache). The same 36 layers as a single group give only ~17,579 blocks. So this is not straightforward to reproduce with a stock uniform model on one 80 GB card — hence snippet (b), which exercises the kernel-level mechanism directly and needs neither vLLM nor weights. In memory terms the bound is `4 GiB * group_size` of KV cache per pool group (bf16, this layout). Two-mode summary: | condition | result | | --- | --- | | block id < bound | correct | | block id ≥ bound, wrapped address unmapped | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` | | block id ≥ bound, wrapped address **mapped** | **no error — silently reads the neighbouring allocation, wrong output** | Consistent with a latent bound rather than a workload issue: everything that appeared to "fix" it — lowering `gpu_memory_utilization`, capping `max_num_seqs`, enabling eviction, `PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING=1` — merely keeps the allocator from handing out block ids at the top of the pool. ### Upstream status The int32 offset arithmetic itself lives in PyTorch's generated FlexAttention kernel and **has since been fixed**: [pytorch#190857](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/190857) (closed) and [PR #185264](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/185264), which adds an `INDEX_DTYPE` parameter to `load_checked_2d` and casts the offsets before they are multiplied by strides, at every call site in the forward, backward and common templates. So on a torch that carries #185264 this should no longer be reachable, even with int32 `kv_indices`. It remains reachable on releases without it — ours (`2.11.0+cu128`) has `INDEX_DTYPE` appearing zero times in `torch/_inductor/kernel/flex/templates/utilities.py.jinja`. ### Suggested mitigations on the vLLM side 1. **Validate at start-up** (cheap, no perf impact): warn or clamp when `num_gpu_blocks` exceeds `2**31 // (block_size * kv_packing * num_kv_heads * head_size)` and the running torch lacks the fix. We do this out-of-tree by wrapping `kv_cache_utils.may_override_num_blocks`; it cost 4.1% of pool capacity (70,315 → 65,536 blocks, 243,350 → 233,263 tokens) with no measurable throughput change, and it removed both failure modes. 2. Or declare a **minimum torch version** for the FlexAttention backend. 3. Optionally, a **non-interleaved** K/V layout for this backend — halving the row stride doubles the bound regardless of the torch version. FWIW the `persistent_rswa_kv_indices` comment in the same file already documents an adjacent hazard ("... producing an out-of-bounds K/V pointer and a CUDA illegal memory access") and fixes it for the R-SWA path only; this report is the non-R-SWA path with a different mechanism. - [x] Searched existing issues (found none covering the int32 index bound; #13824 / #23814 / #33242 / #35706 / #39025 are unrelated illegal-memory-access reports)

items.title: VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND env var is silently ignored — attention_backend= LLM()/EngineArgs kwarg is the only mechanism that works
items.body:
### Your current environment

vLLM 0.26.0, single GPU (Ampere, sm_86), WSL2/Ubuntu, V1 engine.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Setting the environment variable `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND` before constructing `LLM(...)` has **no effect** — the engine silently falls through to its own default backend selection, with no warning or error indicating the env var was unrecognized. Confirmed via `grep -rl ATTENTION_BACKEND` across the entire installed `vllm` package (0.26.0): the literal string does not appear anywhere in the source, so nothing reads it.

The only mechanism that actually works in the current V1 engine is the `attention_backend=` keyword argument to `LLM()` (equivalently `EngineArgs.attention_backend`, an `AttentionBackendEnum | None`).

This name is still commonly referenced in tutorials, blog posts, and older Stack Overflow answers (presumably from a pre-V1 vLLM version where it may have worked), so a user following that guidance today gets silently the wrong backend with zero indication anything went wrong.

### Minimal repro

```python
import os
os.environ["VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND"] = "TRITON_ATTN"

from vllm import LLM
llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", gpu_memory_utilization=0.5)
# Log shows: "Using AttentionBackendEnum.FLASH_ATTN backend."
# NOT TRITON_ATTN, and no warning that the env var was ignored.
```

versus the mechanism that actually works:

```python
from vllm import LLM
llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", gpu_memory_utilization=0.5, attention_backend="TRITON_ATTN")
# Log shows: "Using AttentionBackendEnum.TRITON_ATTN backend."
```

### Suggested fix

Either:
- (a) restore `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND` as a supported alias for `attention_backend=` (simplest, preserves backward compatibility with existing tutorials/docs referencing it), or
- (b) if the env var is intentionally no longer supported, emit a `logger.warning` when it's set but unused, so misconfiguration is visible instead of silent.

### Context

Found while running a controlled factorial experiment (attention backend as one of several independent variables) in an unrelated measurement project — caught only because the experimental effect for that factor came back suspiciously exactly zero across every paired comparison, which prompted a source-level check. Without that scrutiny this would have silently invalidated the results attributed to that factor.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Searched existing issues/PRs for `VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND` and `attention_backend` — found related-but-distinct items (e.g. DCP error-message PRs referencing the name), none reporting this specific silent-no-op behavior.

items.title: [Core] Add --enable-nan-fault-tolerance for NaN detection and request abort
items.body:
## Summary

- Adds `--enable-detect-nans-in-logits` CLI flag (replaces `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` env var with a proper engine arg, keeps env var for backward compat)
- Adds `--enable-nan-fault-tolerance` CLI flag which implies `--enable-detect-nans-in-logits` and additionally:
  - **Aborts requests** when NaN values are detected in logits — during chunked prefill intermediate chunks, final chunks, or decode steps
  - **Forces KV cache block zeroing** on reuse (`needs_kv_cache_zeroing` returns `True`) to prevent stale NaN data from being read by subsequent requests
  - **Evicts the aborted request's blocks from the prefix cache** so a NaN-corrupted block that prefill committed to the cache cannot be matched (and read) as a prefix-cache hit by a later request with the same prefix

## Motivation

Currently, `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS=1` only flags corrupted requests as a Prometheus metric (`vllm:corrupted_requests`). The request continues running to completion, meaning:

- Corrupted KV cache blocks can be reused via prefix caching
- NaN KV data gets offloaded to CPU/disk tiers
- In disaggregated PD, corrupted KV is transferred per-layer to decode instances via NIXL before the NaN is even detected in logits

This PR adds a fault-tolerance mode that aborts requests on NaN detection and zeroes freed blocks on reallocation, preventing corruption from propagating.

## Known Limitations

- NIXL transfers KV per-layer during the forward pass (`save_kv_layer`). By the time NaN is detected in logits (post-forward), the current step's KV may already be on the decode instance. The abort prevents future steps but cannot recall already-transferred data.
- The KV cache for the chunk that produced NaN is already written. Abort evicts those blocks from the prefix cache (so they can't be matched as a hit) and zeroing wipes them on reallocation.
- Detection is on logits. If a NaN corrupts the KV of a *decode* step, that step's token is not committed to the prefix cache before the abort frees the request, so decode-phase NaN blocks never become matchable. The prefix-cache exposure is specific to prefill, where full blocks are committed at schedule time — which is exactly what the eviction closes.

## End-to-end testing guide

Verified on the default (V2) GPU model runner with **async scheduling** using `Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B`. A healthy model rarely emits NaN logits on demand, so both tests use a one-line debug edit to force a NaN, then observe the two behaviors the flag controls: (A) the request is **aborted**, and (B) the freed KV blocks are **zeroed on reuse**.

### Part A — NaN in logits aborts the request

**1. Force a NaN.** In `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/sampler.py`, inside `Sampler.__call__`, add one line immediately before:

```python
        num_nans = get_num_nans(logits) if self.compute_nans else None
```

so it reads:

```python
        logits[-1, 0] = float("nan")  # debug: force a NaN
        num_nans = get_num_nans(logits) if self.compute_nans else None
```

**2. Start the server** (async scheduling on):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B \
    --enable-nan-fault-tolerance \
    --async-scheduling \
    --max-model-len 2048
```

The startup config confirms the implication: `enable_detect_nans_in_logits=True, enable_nan_fault_tolerance=True`.

**3. Send a request:**

```bash
curl -s -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:8000/v1/completions \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":20,"temperature":0}'
```

Expected — the request is aborted instead of returning a (corrupt) completion:

```
HTTP=500
# engine log:
WARNING [scheduler.py] Request <id> aborted: 1 NaN values in logits
```

**Control:** restart the same server **without** `--enable-nan-fault-tolerance` (keeping the debug line). The identical request now returns `HTTP=200` with a normal completion — the NaN is counted in the metric but the request is not aborted.

### Part B — freed KV blocks are zeroed on reuse

The flag also makes `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` return `True`, so every block is zeroed when it is (re)allocated to a request — the block a NaN-aborted request wrote is wiped before another request can reuse it. It does **not** zero the whole KV cache (that would be prohibitively expensive); it zeroes exactly the blocks each request touches, at allocation time.

**1. Observe the zeroing.** In `vllm/v1/worker/utils.py`, add a print at the top of `KVBlockZeroer.zero_block_ids`:

```python
    def zero_block_ids(self, block_ids: list[int]) -> None:
        """Zero the KV cache memory for the given block IDs."""
        print(f"[kv-zero] zeroing {len(block_ids)} block(s): {block_ids[:8]}", flush=True)  # debug
        if not block_ids or self._meta is None:
            return
```

**2. Serve with the flag** (keep the Part A NaN injection so requests abort and free their blocks):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B --enable-nan-fault-tolerance --async-scheduling --max-model-len 2048
```

**3. Send a short and a long prompt:**

```bash
# short prompt (fits in one 16-token block)
curl -s -o /dev/null http://localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B","prompt":"The capital of France is","max_tokens":20,"temperature":0}'

# long prompt (spans several blocks)
curl -s -o /dev/null http://localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B","prompt":"Please summarize in great detail the following passage and then continue the narrative: once upon a time in a distant kingdom by the sea there lived a wise old scholar who studied the stars and the tides","max_tokens":16,"temperature":0}'
```

Expected — the number of zeroed blocks scales with each request's block footprint (block 0 is the reserved null block, so allocation starts at block 1). Each aborted request frees its blocks, and the next request re-zeroes them on reallocation:

```
[kv-zero] zeroing 1 block(s): [1]              # short prompt
[kv-zero] zeroing 4 block(s): [1, 2, 3, 4]     # long prompt
```

**Control:** restart **without** `--enable-nan-fault-tolerance`. `needs_kv_cache_zeroing` is `False`, so `[kv-zero]` never prints — no blocks are zeroed and requests complete normally.

### Part C — an aborted request's blocks are evicted from the prefix cache

This is the correctness case the eviction closes: prefill commits a full block to the prefix cache **at schedule time, before the forward writes KV**. If that forward produces NaN, the block is already matchable. The abort must evict it, or a later request with the same prefix would reuse the NaN KV as a cache hit (hits are never re-zeroed).

To make the NaN fire on a *real* request (not warmup, which also runs the sampler), arm it from a file instead of the always-on line in Part A. In `Sampler.__call__`, immediately before the `num_nans = ...` line:

```python
        import os as _dbg_os
        if _dbg_os.path.exists("/tmp/arm_nan"):
            _dbg_os.remove("/tmp/arm_nan")
            logits[-1, 0] = float("nan")  # debug: one real-request NaN
```

Add a log line at the top of `KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks` to observe prefix-cache reuse, and one in `BlockPool.evict_blocks`:

```python
# get_computed_blocks, right before `return blocks, num_new_computed_tokens, ...`
        print(f"[prefix-hit] req={request.request_id} new_computed_tokens={num_new_computed_tokens}", flush=True)
# evict_blocks, first line
        print(f"[evict] block_ids={sorted(block_ids)}", flush=True)
```

Serve with the flag, then send the **same** prompt twice — the first arms and aborts, the second reuses (or, with the fix, does not):

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B --enable-nan-fault-tolerance --async-scheduling --max-model-len 2048

P="The capital of France is Paris and the capital of Germany is Berlin and the capital of Italy is Rome and the capital of Spain is"
touch /tmp/arm_nan
curl -s -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"model\":\"Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B\",\"prompt\":\"$P\",\"max_tokens\":10,\"temperature\":0}"   # request #1
curl -s -w '\nHTTP=%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"model\":\"Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B\",\"prompt\":\"$P\",\"max_tokens\":10,\"temperature\":0}"   # request #2
```

Expected — request #1 aborts (`HTTP=500`), its blocks are evicted, and request #2 gets **no** prefix-cache reuse of the NaN block:

```
[dbg-nan] ...                         # on request #1's forward
WARNING [scheduler.py] Request <id-1> aborted: 1 NaN values in logits
[evict] block_ids=[1, 2]              # NaN block(s) evicted from the prefix cache
[prefix-hit] req=<id-2> new_computed_tokens=0   # request #2 recomputes; does NOT reuse the NaN block
HTTP=200                              # request #2 completes cleanly
```

**Control:** temporarily disable the eviction (`if False and nan_block_ids:`). `[evict]` no longer prints and request #2 shows `new_computed_tokens=16` — it matches and reuses the block request #1 wrote during the NaN step. That reuse is exactly what the eviction prevents.

## Test plan

- [x] `--enable-nan-fault-tolerance` implies `--enable-detect-nans-in-logits` (confirmed in startup config)
- [x] NaN in logits aborts the request (`FINISHED_ERROR` → `HTTP 500`) on the default V2 runner, with `--async-scheduling`
- [x] Without the flag, a NaN-producing request completes normally (control)
- [x] Freed KV blocks are zeroed on reuse when the flag is enabled; not zeroed without it (control)
- [x] An aborted request's blocks are evicted from the prefix cache — a later same-prefix request does not reuse the NaN block (`new_computed_tokens=0` with the fix vs `16` without)
- [ ] Verify abort works during intermediate chunked prefill (discarded logits still trigger abort)
- [ ] Verify existing `VLLM_COMPUTE_NANS_IN_LOGITS` env var still works (backward compat)
- [ ] Run existing scheduler and model runner tests for regressions

AI assistance: Claude Opus 4.8.

items.title: [Kernel] Harden top_k_per_row against NaN and under-filled output
items.body:
## Purpose

Addresses the kernel-hardening portion of #49896: prevent `top_k_per_row_prefill` (and the shared `topKPerRowJob` used by the decode/split variants) from emitting uninitialized or invalid indices when NaN values leave fewer than `top_k` selectable candidates.

Root cause in `csrc/libtorch_stable/sampler.cu`: `extractBinIdx` bins positive-NaN bit patterns above +inf, so NaN-dominated rows place the histogram threshold bin on a NaN bin; the insertion-sort final pass's NaN comparisons all evaluate false, so every threshold-bin element writes slot 0 and the remaining `smemOutput` slots keep uninitialized dynamic shared memory, which the unconditional final store loop emits as indices. With fewer than `top_k` non-NaN candidates, `smemThresholdBinIdx` is additionally read unset. Downstream gathers with the garbage indices then hit device-side asserts / illegal memory access.

Changes (kernel `+42/−1`, tests `+209`):
- `isNaNLogit()` bit-pattern test (robust under `--use_fast_math`, HIP-compatible via `__float_as_uint`);
- NaN exclusion in both `distributeToBins` and `processBins`, kept consistent so histogram counts match prefix sums;
- well-defined fallback when fewer than `top_k` candidates exist (`smemThresholdBinIdx = kNumBins`, `smemFinalBinSize = 0`);
- `smemOutput` pre-filled with `-1` (multi-block variant also `-FLT_MAX` logit halves), `finalIndices[ii] = -1` init in the radix path, and a `-1`-preserving rebase in the strided final store — under-filled rows now return `-1` padding like the short-row path instead of garbage.

Scope notes:
- This does not change DeepSeek-V4 routing (#49897 territory), the upstream NaN source (DeepGEMM side), or the downstream gather.
- The short-row path (`rowLen <= topK`) keeps its documented "return all candidate positions" behavior (memory-safe); #49897's torch fallback excludes NaN even for short rows — deliberate, called out for reviewers.

## Test Plan

Hardware: H200 / SM90 (driver 580.65.06), CUDA 13.0 (nvcc 13.0.48), torch 2.13.0+cu130, kernel built from source (`_C_stable_libtorch`) for both parent and patched in the same job/toolchain, on top of current main (`7f4c52f2`). The defect is data-driven (NaN input), per the issue not SM120-specific — confirmed: the unmodified kernel fails identically on H200.

- Canary: the issue's reproduction (clean vs 83%-NaN logits; output prefilled with `-7`, checking garbage / unwritten / out-of-range / NaN-selected rows).
- New tests in `tests/kernels/test_top_k_per_row.py`: 16 NaN cases covering prefill insertion-sort and radix-sort variants (4869-row and 12544-row shapes) and decode insertion / radix / split+merge (8192 / 16384 / 250000), NaN fractions 0.5 / 0.83 / 1.0, asserting: all indices in `[-1, rowLen)`, no unwritten sentinel survives, exactly `min(top_k, num_finite)` valid indices with `-1` suffix padding, and selected values equal to a NaN-excluded `torch.topk` reference.
- Regression: full existing `test_top_k_per_row.py`.
- `compute-sanitizer` memcheck on the canary + prefill NaN + decode NaN cases, and initcheck on the canary (patched build).

## Test Result

| Input | Parent (unpatched) | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| clean finite | 166 passed / 6 skipped (reference set-equality) | 166 passed / 6 skipped — unchanged |
| partial NaN, finite ≥ k | NaN tests FAILED (wrong/garbage sets) | 16 passed — finite-only top-k equals reference |
| partial NaN, finite < k | canary: device-side assert (`AcceleratorError`); NaN tests FAILED | canary PASS (`garbage_rows=0 unwritten_rows=0 nan_selected_hist_rows=0 out_of_range_rows=0`); tests assert finite indices + `-1` padding |
| all NaN | NaN tests FAILED (garbage/NaN-bit indices) | 16 passed — all `-1` on histogram rows |

- New NaN tests: parent 16 failed → patched 16 passed (identical test code, same job).
- `compute-sanitizer`: memcheck ×3 and initcheck ×1 all `ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors`.
- Reverse A/B on the pre-rebase tree: unpatched `.so` swapped back → 16 failed; patched restored → canary PASS.

items.body:
Stabilizes the ROCm `test_ngram_and_suffix_correctness` group after the intermittent AMD CI failure in [Buildkite build 11367](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11367/list?jid=019fa7f3-f1e7-4758-a230-01d7b66fed3e&tab=output). The failing run completed the ngram case, force-killed its engine after the five-second shutdown window, and then failed in the suffix case with an asynchronous GPU fault. The retry passed, so this PR does not claim a confirmed production-kernel root cause. It isolates persistent compile artifacts and makes engine teardown explicit for this test.

- Applies `disable_vllm_compile_cache` only when `current_platform.is_rocm()`.
- The existing fixture creates fresh Inductor and Triton cache directories.
- It also sets `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1`, preventing reuse of vLLM's on-disk compile artifacts.
- Runs each parametrized engine through the existing `VllmRunner` context manager.
- This gives ROCm up to 60 seconds for graceful engine-core shutdown.
- It performs the existing distributed cleanup and waits for ROCm memory to settle before the next engine starts.

items.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Fix NaN handling in rejection sampler tl.argmax
items.body:
## Summary

`tl.argmax` on an all-NaN block returns an out-of-range block index (pointing into the padded region beyond `num_blocks - 1`). That index is used to load from the local-argmax tensor, producing an out-of-bounds read and an illegal memory access downstream in the rejection sampler.

Two kernels in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler_utils.py` are affected:

- `_compute_global_target_argmax` — `tl.argmax(local_max)` at line 111, result used to index `target_local_argmax_ptr` at line 113.
- `_insert_resampled_kernel` — `tl.argmax(resampled_local_max)` at line 852, result used to index `resampled_local_argmax_ptr` at line 854.

When all values in the (padded) block dimension are NaN — reachable via NaN target logits — `tl.argmax` does not guarantee an in-range result. The loaded garbage index then propagates into subsequent gathers/stores, surfacing as an illegal memory access.

**Fix:** in both kernels, map NaN to `-inf` via `tl.where` before `tl.argmax`, and clamp the resulting block index to `num_blocks - 1` with `tl.minimum` as a defensive bound. Two small, surgical changes; no behavior change for non-NaN inputs.

## Symptom / reproduction

Observed as an illegal memory access during speculative-decoding warmup (DSpark) when serving Kimi-K3 on 8xB300 with TP=8. Confirmed the root cause with a standalone Triton repro on an RTX 4090:

```python
import torch, triton, triton.language as tl

@triton.jit
def k(out_ptr, NUM_BLOCKS: tl.constexpr, PAD: tl.constexpr):
    blocks = tl.arange(0, PAD)
    vals = tl.full((PAD,), float("nan"), tl.float32)
    vals = tl.where(blocks < NUM_BLOCKS, vals, float("-inf"))
    idx = tl.argmax(vals, axis=0)
    tl.store(out_ptr, idx)

out = torch.empty(1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
k[(1,)](out, NUM_BLOCKS=4, PAD=8)
print(out.item())  # unpatched: 8 (out of range); with NaN->-inf + clamp: in [0, 3]
```

On the all-NaN input, unpatched `tl.argmax` returns `idx == num_blocks` (out of range); with the NaN→-inf mapping plus clamp the index stays in range.

## Validation

- Standalone Triton repro (RTX 4090): patched kernel returns an in-range index on all-NaN input; unpatched does not.
- Full vLLM server on 8xB300, TP=8, Kimi-K3 with DSpark speculative decoding: server boots through warmup (previously IMA), generates coherent output, acceptance length 2.5, conc=1 throughput 110–116 tok/s (+58% vs no-spec).

## Disclosure

- AI assistance (Kimi K3) was used in developing this fix. A human engineer (Gabriel Peracio, Parasail) reviewed every changed line and validated the fix on hardware as described above.
- Checked for duplicates before opening: no open PR or issue covers `tl.argmax`/NaN out-of-bounds in the rejection sampler (`rejection_sampler_utils.py`).

items.title: [Bug]: NVFP4 KV writes V block scales in the SM100 trtllm-gen swizzle unconditionally, silently corrupting the SM120 FlashInfer XQA route
items.body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```
GPU:        NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (32,607 MiB), compute capability 12.0 (SM120)
Driver:     610.62, CUDA 13.0
Host:       Windows + WSL2
vLLM:       v0.25.1 (upstream commit 752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34)
FlashInfer: 0.6.15.post1
PyTorch:    2.11.0+cu130
Power cap:  575 W (default), persistence enabled
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`reshape_and_cache_nvfp4_kernel` writes **K** block scales linearly but writes **V** block scales in the 4×4 swizzle required by the SM100 `trtllm-gen` MHA kernel — **unconditionally, for every architecture**.

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/csrc/libtorch_stable/nvfp4_kv_cache_kernels.cu#L155-L173

```cpp
      // Write block scale to scale cache.
      // K (kv==0): linear layout (no swizzle).
      // V (kv==1): swizzled layout for SM100 trtllm-gen MHA kernel.
      if (sf_out_ptr != nullptr) {
        int scale_idx = group_in_head;
        uint8_t* __restrict__ scale_dst;
        if (kv == 0) {
          ...
        } else {
          int swizzled_offset =
              swizzle_scale_offset(block_offset, scale_idx, scale_dim);
```

On SM120 the NVFP4 KV route (FA2 prefill + FlashInfer **XQA** decode, discussed in #49011) consumes K and V scale tensors through **ordinary NHD tensor strides**. The XQA wrapper takes `[pages, page_size, kv_heads, head_dim/16]` scale tensors and passes the real page/token/head strides straight through; the XQA CUDA code contains **no V-scale de-swizzle**. FlashInfer's own paged-NVFP4 quantizer documents its V-scale swizzle as being *for `trtllm-gen` MHA* — that layout is not the XQA layout.

So the SM120 route wires a **swizzled producer to a linear consumer**. Every tensor has the correct shape, dtype and alignment, no kernel errors, no NaNs — the values are simply read in the wrong order. The result is a silently degraded model rather than a crash.

This is separate from #43562 (trtllm-gen FP4 FMHA has no sm_120 build). It sits *below* the read-side view work in #49011 / #44851 — those fix which kernels get selected and how the views are bound; this is the layout the data was written in to begin with.

---

### Evidence

All probes are model-free: deterministic BF16 inputs written through the installed `reshape_and_cache_flash` binding, then independently unpacked and dequantized.

**1. Synthetic round trip.** Normal NVFP4 loss in this exercise is ≈0.095 relative L2 (what K shows). V is far outside that, and linearizing *only* the V scales restores it:

| KV heads / Q heads | K rel-L2 | V rel-L2 (current) | V rel-L2 (scales linearized) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 / 8 | 0.0952 | **0.7625** | 0.0953 |
| 2 / 16 | 0.0954 | **0.7615** | 0.0949 |
| 4 / 24 | 0.0948 | **0.7876** | 0.0957 |
| 8 / 48 | 0.0946 | **0.7649** | 0.0953 |

No NaN/Inf. Per-head matching selected the identity mapping in all cases; no head swap.

**2. Direct XQA.** Two pages, page size 16, non-trivial block table `[1, 0]`, sequence length 23 — so page metadata and indexing are exercised too:

| KV heads / Q heads | current vs correct ref | current vs *deliberately wrong-scale* ref | linear-V vs correct ref |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 / 8 | 0.8222 | **0.00211** | 0.00213 |
| 2 / 16 | 0.7861 | **0.00218** | 0.00219 |
| 4 / 24 | 0.7769 | **0.00216** | 0.00216 |
| 8 / 48 | 0.7453 | **0.00214** | 0.00212 |

XQA reproduces almost exactly a reference that *deliberately applies the current wrong V-scale order*. That isolates the failure to the layout contract, ahead of the XQA math kernel.

**3. Not a striding/contiguity artifact.** Copying the four split views into explicit contiguous buffers changed direct-XQA output by **exactly zero** for every head count. Changing only V scale values from swizzled to linear corrected it. Adding copies does not help.

**4. It is not two-KV-head specific.** Both 2 and 4 KV heads fail the same structural test and both recover when V scales are linear. A checkpoint that appeared healthy on this route was not evidence the layout was valid — it was less likely to expose the corruption on the prompts being run.

---

### Correction to an earlier characterization of mine

I want this on the record because I stated it publicly and it was wrong.

In my first write-up (comment on #49011, and a downstream discussion thread) I described the V write as **destructive** — "V stored only the first four source scales replicated across groups of four; twelve of sixteen values lost at write time." **That is incorrect.** It was an artifact of inspecting only token row 0.

The 4×4 transform is a **lossless bijection** jointly across token and scale-group coordinates — the other source scale groups are present, in destination token rows 1–3:

```
dest_token = (src_token // 4) * 4 + src_scale // (num_scales // 4)
dest_scale = (src_scale % (num_scales // 4)) * 4 + src_token % 4
```

Confirmation: the full 16-token × 16-scale plane contains all 15 representable distinct FP8 values from the structured probe (the nominal 13th and 14th both round to 2.25). Applying the joint inverse restores V stored-order relative L2 from **0.588793 → 0.026317**, *exactly* matching K.

The practical consequence is unchanged — SM120 reads V scales in the wrong order and the model degrades — but "information is destroyed at write time" and "information is permuted into a layout this consumer doesn't undo" are different bugs with different fixes, and only the second one is real. I'd rather correct it here than have a reviewer inherit the wrong mental model.

---

### Proposed fix

Keep the swizzle where its consumer needs it, and write linear V scales where the consumer reads linearly. Compile-time, no runtime cost, K unchanged:

```cpp
#if defined(__CUDA_ARCH__) && \
    (__CUDA_ARCH__ == 1200 || __CUDA_ARCH__ == 1210)
        constexpr bool swizzle_v_scale = false;
#else
        constexpr bool swizzle_v_scale = true;
#endif
        if (kv == 0 || !swizzle_v_scale) {
          // linear
        } else {
          // existing TRT-LLM swizzle
        }
```

After rebuilding the corrected writer, stored V relative L2 is 0.026317 for both 2 and 4 KV heads — exactly matching K — and applying the *old* inverse transform now damages it to 0.592983, i.e. the layout really did flip. Integrated re-validation across KV heads 1/2/4/8:

| KV heads | K rel-L2 | patched V rel-L2 | XQA vs ref | strided vs contiguous |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 0.09517 | 0.09530 | 0.002135 | 0 |
| 2 | 0.09542 | 0.09493 | 0.002194 | 0 |
| 4 | 0.09478 | 0.09568 | 0.002159 | 0 |
| 8 | 0.09457 | 0.09533 | 0.002121 | 0 |

I'll follow up with a PR referencing this issue. It also tightens the kernel tests, which currently pass with a loose elementwise tolerance that this class of layout error slips straight through — they should assert the expected layout per capability and carry a relative-L2 regression guard.

### End-to-end effect

150-scenario agentic/quality benchmark suites on a Qwen3.6-derived 27B NVFP4 checkpoint over the SM120 NVFP4-KV route, thinking-on, two draws per arm.

The **matched** comparison — same night, same image, same 131,072 context / 8 GiB pinned KV / 6 sequences, changing only `--kv-cache-dtype`:

| KV dtype (post-fix writer) | draws | mean |
|---|---|--:|
| FP8 E4M3 (control) | 121, 122 | 121.5 / 150 |
| **NVFP4** | 121, 124 | **122.5 / 150** |

Post-fix, FP4 KV lands on top of its FP8 control rather than below it.

For context — and I'll flag the confound rather than hide it — the same checkpoint on the **pre-fix** writer scored a 116/150 mean (232/300 at `--repeat 2`). That run used a 262,144 context envelope rather than 131,072, so it is *not* a matched arm and I won't claim the delta as a clean measurement. What it does indicate is direction: pre-fix, this route sat below its own FP8 control and read as ordinary quantization cost.

The wider point for anyone triaging this: the defect was silently costing quality on a configuration that passed every smoke test, needle-in-a-haystack retrieval to 246K tokens, and 1h40m of continuous load without a single error. There is no failure signature to grep for.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] I have made sure to search the existing issues and this is not a duplicate. This is distinct from #43562 (missing sm_120 trtllm-gen FMHA build) and sits below the read-side routing work in #49011 / #44851.
